slides.0.title: Coastal Region II: Paarl, Franschhoek, Constantia, Durbanville
slides.0.subtitle: Four very different places
slides.1.title: Paarl and Franschhoek
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Paarl
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About 50 km north-east of Cape Town, named for Paarl Rock (paarl = pearl); the town dates from 1690 and KWV was based here from 1918; further inland and warmer than Stellenbosch, with Syrah, Chenin Blanc and Pinotage prominent
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Wellington splits off
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wellington became its own District on 21 September 2012
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Franschhoek Valley
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A Ward of Paarl from the 1973 demarcation until 2010, when it became a District; about 1,254 ha; around 200 Huguenots arrived from April 1688; old-vine Semillon (such as the 1902 Eikehof block) and Cap Classique are specialities
slides.1.content: Franschhoek is the heart of Huguenot history and became a District only in 2010.
slides.2.title: Constantia and Durbanville
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The Cape Town District
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Created in 2017 and containing four Wards, including Constantia and Durbanville (Constantia, Durbanville, Hout Bay, Philadelphia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Constantia
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Cool and maritime with about 1,000 mm of rain; Sauvignon Blanc is the flagship and Semillon is also important; Vin de Constance is made from Muscat de Frontignan, with Klein Constantia's modern version first made in 1986 and released in 1990
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Durbanville
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Demarcated in 1989 within Tygerberg and moved into the Cape Town District in June 2017; about 12 km from the Atlantic; Sauvignon Blanc is the identity grape; vineyards lie at about 100–240 m
slides.2.content: Both are important for Sauvignon Blanc, but Constantia is cooler and wetter and carries the history of Vin de Constance.
Franschhoek was a Ward of which district before 2010?
Paarl; it became a District in 2010.
Which variety is Vin de Constance made from?
Muscat de Frontignan (Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains).
Since 2017 Constantia and Durbanville belong to which District?
The Cape Town District; Durbanville was previously in Tygerberg.
In which year did Wellington become its own District?
